Elements in Earth's Crust
Most abundant element in Earth's crust: Oxygen (≈46.6%)
2nd most abundant: Silicon (≈27.7%)
3rd most abundant: Aluminium (≈8.1%)
Types of Rocks
Igneous Rocks - formed from cooling magma/lava → Example: Basalt, Granite
Sedimentary Rocks - formed from deposition of material → Example: Limestone, Sandstone
Metamorphic Rocks - formed from heat/pressure on other rocks → Example: Marble, Slate
Earth's 4 Layers
Crust - outermost; solid; we live on it
Mantle - semi-solid; rich in silicates of magnesium and iron
Outer Core - liquid; mostly iron & nickel
Inner Core - solid; hottest part (~6000°C)
4 Layers of the Atmosphere
Troposphere - 0 to ~12 km; weather occurs here, airplanes fly here; T= -50°C
Stratosphere - 12-50 km; contains ozone layer; T= -3°C
Mesosphere - 50-80 km; meteors burn here; T= -90°C
Thermosphere - 80 km+; auroras & satellites here; T= +1500°C

Primary Pollutants - Which are directly emitted: CO, SO₂, NO, Particulate Matter 10 (PM 10), VOCs (VOCs are produced via paints, pesticides)
Sources of Primary Pollutants - Vehicles, industries, power plants, wildfires
Secondary Pollutants - Formed in atmosphere: Ozone (O₃), Smog, Acid Rain
Ozone Depletion Causes - Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), Halons, HCFCs (Hydrochlorofluorocarbons) *Refrigerators, Fire Extinguishers, Spray Cans and Foam Production produces it.

Smog Is - Smoke + Fog

Climate Change (CC) - Long-term shift in global or regional climate patterns
Global Warming - Rise in Earth's average surface temperature due to GHGs
Normal Atmospheric Temp. - ~15°C (average global temperature)
Causes of CC - Greenhouse gases, deforestation, industrialization, burning fossil fuels
Proofs of CC - Glacial melt, rising sea levels, extreme weather, wildfires, shifting agricultural patterns, heat waves.
GHG - Major Source
Water Vapors - Evaporation. Most abundant source.
CO₂ - Fossil fuel combustion (vehicles, industries)
CH₄ - Agriculture (rice fields, livestock), landfills
N₂O - Fertilizers used in agriculture
CFCs - Refrigerants, aerosol sprays (now banned under Montreal Protocol)
O₃ - Formed in troposphere from chemical reactions involving NOx and VOCs
Agreement - Description
Kyoto Protocol (1997) *Ratified in 2005 - First binding treaty to reduce GHGs. Introduced CDM, JI, ERU mechanisms Decrease in GHG emissions by 5% of 1990 levels. (Failed)
Doha Amendment (2012)
Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) - Developed countries invest in green projects in developing countries
Joint Implementation (JI) - Emission reduction projects among developed countries
Emission Reduction Units (ERU) - Tradable credit for each ton of GHG reduced
Montreal Protocol (1987) - Banned Ozone-depleting substances (like CFCs)
UNFCCC (1992) - Framework convention to stabilize GHG emissions
Paris Agreement (2015) - Limit global warming below 2°C, ideally 1.5°C of Pre- Industrialization levels.
COPs (Conferences of Parties) - Annual climate summits under UNFCCC framework

Climate Justice - Principle that those least responsible for climate change suffer the most

Preservation Method; Main Principle; Examples
Refrigeration; Low temperature slows microbial growth; Milk, fruits, vegetables
Freezing; Stops microbial activity by freezing water; Meat, peas, ice cream
Drying/Dehydration; Removes moisture to inhibit microbes; Dates, spices, dried fish
Canning; Heating and sealing in airtight containers; Pickles, jams, beans
Salting; Removes moisture & inhibits microbes; Salted fish, pickles
Sugaring; High sugar creates osmotic pressure; Jams, jellies, candied fruits
Fermentation; Good bacteria produce acids/alcohol; Yogurt, sauerkraut
Pasteurization; Controlled heating to kill pathogens *Heat at 72°C for 15 seconds Or 138-150°C for 1-2 seconds Or 63°C for 30 minutes; Milk, juices
Vacuum Packing; Removes oxygen to slow spoilage; Packaged meats, coffee
Irradiation; Uses radiation to kill microbes/insects; Spices, dried herbs

Disease: Dengue; Cause (Pathogen): Dengue virus (Flavivirus); Transmission: Aedes mosquito bite; Key Symptoms: High fever, joint pain, rash, bleeding; Prevention: Avoid mosquito bites, clean environment; Vaccine Available: (Dengvaxia)

Disease: Malaria; Cause (Pathogen): Plasmodium parasite; Transmission: Anopheles mosquito bite; Key Symptoms: Fever with chills, sweating, body ache; Prevention: Mosquito nets, antimalarials; Vaccine Available: (RTS,S)/ Mosquirix

Disease: Hepatitis B; Cause (Pathogen): Hepatitis B virus; Transmission: Blood, unprotected sex, needles; Key Symptoms: Liver damage, jaundice, chronic illness; Prevention: Vaccination, avoid sharing needles; Vaccine Available: Engerix-B

Disease: Hepatitis C; Cause (Pathogen): Hepatitis C virus; Transmission: Blood transfusion, needles; Key Symptoms: Often silent early, chronic liver issues; Prevention: Safe injections, screen blood; Vaccine Available: No

Disease: AIDS (HIV); Cause (Pathogen): HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus); Transmission: Blood, sex, mother to child; Key Symptoms: Weak immunity, infections, weight loss; Prevention: Safe sex, screened blood; Vaccine Available: No

Disease: Diarrhoea; Cause (Pathogen): Various (bacteria/viruses); Transmission: Contaminated food/water; Key Symptoms: Loose stools, dehydration, weakness; Prevention: Clean water, hygiene, ORS; Vaccine Available: (Rotavirus vaccine - for viral type)

Disease: Polio; Cause (Pathogen): Poliovirus; Transmission: Fecal-oral, contaminated water; Key Symptoms: Paralysis, fever, muscle weakness; Prevention: Polio drops (OPV), sanitation; Vaccine Available: (OPV & IPV)

Bond Type: Ionic Bond; One-liner Definition: Formed by transfer of electrons between metals and non-metals.; Examples: NaCl (Sodium Chloride), CaCl₂
Bond Type: Covalent Bond; One-liner Definition: Formed by sharing of electron pairs between atoms (usually non-metals).; Examples: H₂O (Water), CO₂, CH₄ (Methane), NH₃, O₂, Cl₂
Bond Type: Metallic Bond; One-liner Definition: Positive metal ions surrounded by a sea of delocalized electrons.; Examples: Fe (Iron), Cu (Copper), Al (Aluminum), Zn (Zinc)
Bond Type: Coordinate Covalent; One-liner Definition: Shared electrons both come from the same atom (donor → acceptor).; Examples: NH₄⁺ (Ammonium), CO (Carbon monoxide), H₃O⁺
Bond Type: Hydrogen Bond; One-liner Definition: Weak bond between H and electronegative atoms (F, O, N) - not a true bond, but strong IMF.; Examples: H₂O, HF, NH₃
Type: Dipole-Dipole; Definition: Attraction between polar molecules due to their dipole moments.; Example: Hydrogen chloride (HCl)
Type: Hydrogen Bonding; Definition: Special case of dipole-dipole, where hydrogen is bonded to electronegative atoms (F, O, N).; Example: Water (H₂O)
Type: Van der Waals; Definition: Weak attraction between nonpolar molecules due to instantaneous dipoles.; Example: Oxygen (O₂), Nitrogen (N₂)

Energy Type - How It Is Formed
Kinetic Energy - Energy of a moving object; formed when an object is in motion due to a force.
Gravitational Potential Energy (GPE) - Stored energy due to an object's position above the ground; increases with height and mass.
Thermal Energy (Heat Energy) - Formed due to movement of particles in a substance; generated by friction, combustion, or chemical reactions.
Chemical Energy - Stored in chemical bonds; released during chemical reactions (e.g., in batteries, food, fuel).
Electrical Energy - Formed by the movement of electrons; generated using turbines, batteries, or solar cells.
Nuclear Energy - Formed from nuclear fission (splitting atoms) or fusion (joining atoms), releasing massive energy.
Elastic Potential Energy - Stored in stretched or compressed objects like springs or rubber bands.
Sound Energy - Produced by vibrations; travels in waves through a medium.
